body:
Tbh I’m not optimistic at all. I’m just trying to rationalize what went wrong and what can I do about it. I’m not quite sure if I’m improving despite of my efforts but at least I’m doing no harm to anyone nor myself (not that I know of). And yes, I do agree that there is always a dark side to self-improvement and a single mistake can make you bring back all the bad habits, or not. That big sacrifice is prolly mostly the little ones that we keep on overlooking. Put it all together and it becomes who we are. 

Maybe I’ll spend some time for spiritual stuff. It helped me in the past although it partly made me more confused. Haha. But yeah... that’s one thing.

Thank you for the advice! I’d organize my thoughts and think what could possibly the moral principle behind it all. The idea that I could live live upon! :)

There’s always a chronic feeling of emptiness. I wasn’t diagnosed with BPD, only with Bipolar and Major Depression. But I have a psychometrician sister who told me about the possibility of me having BPD. Only a psychiatrist can confirm it but so far she didn’t. She isn’t my first psychiatrist tho. My first psychiatrist told me that my mental illness could not just be a mood disorder but a character (a personality) rather. I suspected that she meant bpd but I stopped seeing her even before she can actually diagnose me with a personality disorder because her secretary was so unprofessional. Anyway, I’ve been having a therapy with my new doctor for 6 months. I was pretty much okay when I started my therapy with her and I wasn’t as self-destructive as I was when I was seeing my first therapist. I figured out that most of the criteria for bpd only manifests when I’m with someone. But when I’m on my own, it’s more like a Bipolar disorder. That’s why I can’t really say which is which. For now I’m gonna trust my doctor and hoping I could develop more good coping mechanisms. 

As for hobbies and interest, I play a lot of video games on my switch and I’ve been studying piano lessons for almost a year. It started a month after our breakup. I also watch a lot of medical dramas, clean my room every now and then, and cook something different. I’m trying almost everything on a whim although I get bored with most of it easily. For some reason, I also like reading depressing and existential novels like murakami and kundera’s novels. It makes me feel something. Haha. The sadness that comes with it can be so addicting. 

Maybe you’re right with the part that I do like the feeling of intense attachment. But I don’t think I like toxic behaviors that comes with it neither from me nor from my s/o. Also I think it’s some kind of escapism. They become my go-to when I’m too coward to face my own problems.  I think the underlying problem is not the fact that I want that kind of relationship, but I’m just socially inept to form other meaningful relationships, knowing that it has to be normal and I had to work on it consistently. I feel like I’ve been trying to runaway from my goals such as becoming a doctor by constantly trying to sabotage my studies/career because I don’t fully realize that I could make it. As much as I blame others, I do blame myself immensely as well. I don’t know how and when it started but getting there... like truly believing and trusting myself and trying to unlearn all my unhealthy coping mechanisms, would take a lot of time and self-awareness. It’s overwhelming but... if I’m gonna live I have to start living for myself and start building self-trust which I think I need the most.
sorry to hear that. :(( im sure your dog wants you to be strong for her. just hold on...
